full_judgment:
2. In the instant case the facts are not disputed, but only for the sake of convenience we may state some facts for disposal of this Rule. Admittedly, one Mr. Md. Shahabuddin was the original lessee by a 99 years lease deed between DIT (now RAJUK) and original lessee Shahabuddin. Mr. Shahabuddin was residing there with his family members and with the plan approved by RAJUK constructed building on the plot in question. On 10-1-71 Shahabudin entered into an agreement for sale with the present petitioner at a price of Tk. 2,50,000.00. Major portion of the price was paid to Mr. Shahabuddin by the present petitioner. But in spite of that he was delaying to execute and register the sale deed in favour of the petitioner. As a result, the petitioner was compelled to file a suit being Title Suit No. 709 of 1982 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract and ultimately the suit was transferred to the Court of First Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 409 of 1985. In the title suit the defendants Mr. Shahabuddin, the Government of Bangladesh, the Secretary, Ministry of Works, the DIT (now RAJUK) and House Building Finance Corporation were added as defendants. In that case Government as well as DIT appeared and took several adjournments for filing written statements. But ultimately no written statement was filed. As a result, the suit was decreed ex parte on 24-5-89 within the knowledge of the defendants. Thereafter the present petitioner filed a title execution case and in pursuance of the title execution case the sale deed was executed and registered in favour of the petitioner through Court on 23-8-90 and the present petitioner got possession of the property through Court on 13-9-92. 

 4. However, this aspect of the case has not been disputed in any manner whatsoever by the present Respondents. Now, the question arises that after getting a decree in the aforesaid Title Suit and after getting the sale deed registered through court and possession of the property on 13-9-92 the present petitioner filed several applications before the RAJUK for mutation of his name as the lessee of the RAJUK instead of Mr. Shahabuddin. It is alleged that though repeated representations were made, the RAJUK remained silent and did not give any reply to the representations of the present petitioner. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid action, the petitioner moved this application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Mr. Hasan Arif, the learned Advocate appeared for Respondent No. 1 RAJUK and filed an affidavit-in-opposition. It is the case of the petitioner that the right and title of the property in question of Md. Shahabuddin passed to the present petitioner with the decree in the suit for specific performance of contract as well as from the date of registration in the sale deed through Court in favour of the petitioner. Since the right and title of the previous lessee passed to the present petitioner through court, the Respondent No. 1 RAJUK is under legal obligation to mutate the name of the petitioner in the relevant records of the office of the RAJUK. His further submission is that the RAJUK is only entitled to get the transfer fees as required under the rules from the petitioner at the rate which was prevailing in the year 1971 when agreement was entered into and not at the rate when registration of the sale deed through Court on 23-8-90 was made. Mr. Delwar Hossain further submits that as soon as the deed was registered it will take effect from the date of execution of the agreement dated 10-1-71 and as such the petitioner is liable to pay the transfer fee which was prevailing on 10-1-71. 

 7. As regards the transfer of the property in favour of the petitioner, the decree and the title, no dispute has been raised by the respondents. It is not such a contract that the petitioner is not entitled to enforce in writ jurisdiction. Petitioner has not come for enforcement of any contract here. It is his case that he became the lawful lessee of RAJUK and the right and title over the property which the previous lessee had enjoyed had passed to the petitioner legally. It was stipulated in the agreement that at the time of sale of such lease hold property the prior consent of the DIT (RAJUK) would be necessary and the fees for such transfer should be given to RAJUK. But in the instant case the position is otherwise in view of the fact that since the original lessee failed to perform his part of the contract, the petitioner had to file a suit for specific performance of contract and in that suit he got decree and also through execution of the decree he got the sale deed registered through Court, Further, it appears that in that suit the RAJUK (former DIT) and the Government were defendants who appeared on several occasions and filed applications for time. Since the lease hold right and title of the previous lessee legally passed to the present petitioner, he is entitled to get his name mutated in the official record of RAJUK on payment of legal transfer fees and other legal costs as required under the rules.
